line: Haha, when I was younger I used to wonder, like
vault_lines: Haha, when I was younger
meaning:
He’s asking himself why he sings. Is it because he really has a passion for it, or is he trying to use it to meet women?

Ocean looks back to his past. He used to debate whether he sung for the love of music alone, or if he was instead only using it as a means to make himself appear more attractive to the opposite sex. The use of the harsher expletive “bitches” seems forced when contrasted to the more thoughtful lyrics that precede it, possibly hinting that this is an image he feels he must project to highlight his masculinity, and shun the simple sensitivity of loving music. Ocean had not revealed his sexuality to the public at the time of writing this song, which may lend credence to the suggestion that he felt he must pursue the women he attracted and act stereotypically masculine. This could also be an instance of Ocean looking at his younger self and ridiculing those efforts to conceal his sexuality. It may also highlight his possible confusion over his sexuality at that time, or perhaps be examining a point at which in which he believed himself to be heterosexual.

In the end of her research paper, she feels bad for the girls who don’t have the freedom that she has in the U.S. when it comes to marriage, yet is thankful for having the choice to marry based on the concept of love.

In Islamic law, it is highly recommended that a man marries a virgin because a woman is considered “pure” when she’s a virgin; however, culturally speaking, it isn’t as emphasized for men to be virgins until they marry.

Also, in some Islamic societies (as well, to be sure, as certain Christian and Hindu ones), arranged marriages are very popular. Women are forced to marry by a certain age as a common ritual to prevent disgrace and to avoid becoming old maids… and her family makes sure that the man possesses good qualities, is from a good family, etc. The girl usually doesn’t make the decision of whom she marries.

It is also customary in an Islamic country’s culture for a woman to wear a hijab in front of anyone who isn’t an immediate family member; these members include the husband, brother, father, but not the cousin. A hijab is a garment used to wrap around a woman’s face.



Another aspect of life Islam permits for men is to be polygamous (to have more than one spouse at the same time). Men can be married to up to four women simultaneously, while women can only be married to one. However, if the man fears that he shall not be able to deal justly with them, then he should only marry one (Chatper 4: Surat Al-Nisa, Verse 3).



The richness of this particular line comes from the comparison Frank Ocean is making between Western “American” marriages and Islamic marriages. It is almost a common view among westerners that Islamic traditional marriages are too restrictive. Frank Ocean is trying to make us question our own social norms: are the marriages that are socially acceptable in western societies really better than those of other cultures? It would seem he is trying to point out that our point of view is an extreme opposite to that of traditional societies. Being too liberal about marriage creates its own set of social problems.

Frank Ocean waxes poetic on this bridge, exercising the common idiom mind over matter, which refers to discarding of materialistic things in favor of a freer state of mind. He champions this ideology, claiming it works almost as effectively as magic. He himself lives in this train of thought—as a result, he’s able to perform with such a high level of success.

He comes to a fleeting end in the bridge with an existential thought: he suggests that life, no matter how incredible, passes by in the blink of the eye. As a conclusive statement, it’s extremely powerful: Ocean’s telling the listener that they should let go of materialism because life happens too quickly for us to hold onto physical forms of wealth and success.

The line stands in opposition to “Pink Matter,” where Ocean champions “pleasure over matter.” His reprioritization of “mind of matter” now shows us how he considers a metaphysical connection far more potent than a physical one.

This points out to wordplay on “lying” since he apparently isn’t telling the truth. It’s also pretty clear Frank doesn’t actually own a fighter jet, but he accurately compares an unrequited love to having a jet you can’t fly. The cover of the single has Frank’s friend, Raymond Buck, sitting in a Go-Kart, which is a visualization of this line.

However, the motive behind lying is unclear; he could be doing it sarcastically to assert the person he loves them, or it’s his way of wiggling out of a rejection.

line: Yes, of course I remember, how could I forget (How could I forget) How you feel? (How you feel?) You know you were my first time (Time) A new feel (Down) It won’t ever get old, not in my soul, not in my spirit, keep it alive We’ll go down this road ’til it turns from color to black and white
vault_lines: I remember, how could I forget (How could I forget)
meaning:
In his 2012 open letter, Frank Ocean revealed his first love was a man, which asserts the idea that this song is about a male partner:

4 summers ago, I met somebody. I was 19 years old. He was too. We spent that summer, and the summer after, together. Everyday almost. And on the days we were together, time would glide. Most of the day I’d see him, and his smile. I’d hear his conversation and his silence.. until it was time to sleep. Sleep I would often share with him. By the time I realized I was in love, it was malignant. It was hopeless. There was no escaping, no negotiating with the feeling. No choice. It was my first love, it changed my life.

Frank also revealed through the letter that his love seemed unrequited when he confessed his feelings, which he acknowledges here. The entire song seems to take place in a conversation between them after his confession, or perhaps a conversation that Frank desperately wants to have with him but can only initiate in his mind—a conversation in which Frank’s first love seems to deny and diminish Frank’s feelings towards him, with Frank responding sarcastically to assert his love for him. Frank emphasizes that he still remembers his first love can never love him the way he wants, likely in response to him reminding Frank that he does not feel the same way. Regardless, a lovestruck Frank emotionally discloses the “forever” they spend together that he’s been dreaming of, before sadly pointing out once again how he probably hasn’t been thinking that far ahead.

Furthermore, the road changing from color to black and white represents them sticking together until gay people get the right to marry. They’ll wear black and white, like a bride and groom, instead of the rainbow-colored LGBT flag.

To bring the song full circle, the road changing colors is another reference to The Wizard of Oz, in which the movie changes to black and white once Dorothy heads back home from Oz.



Gay marriage was ruled legal nationwide in the US in 2015.

line: A tornado flew around my room before you came Excuse the mess it made, it usually doesn’t rain in Southern California, much like Arizona My eyes don’t shed tears, but boy, they pour
vault_lines: A tornado flew around my room before you came
meaning:
Frank’s room represents his life; he’s well aware it was messy and out of order before he met his significant other, who brought peace into his life. However, they’ve broken up and it makes him cry which is as rare as rain in California and Arizona. Interestingly, it was thought his second LP would be titled Boys Don’t Cry, but it ended up being the name of the magazine that went along with Blonde.

“It Never Rains in Southern California” is a song that tells a story of a musician who moved to Cali in pursuit of a music career. The tornado is one of two references to the classic novel/movie “The Wizard of Oz” in this song, in which the main character Dorothy is swept away into the Land of Oz by a tornado.

Once you put those two references together, and mix water with a tornado, you get a highly influential event that happened to Ocean. After hurricane Katrina hit his hometown of New Orleans, Frank moved to Los Angeles to chase his dream of being a musician.

Furthermore, “It Never Rains in Southern California” contains the following lyrics:

It never rains in California, but girl, don’t they warn ya?
It pours, man, it pours

In the mentioned lines, “girl” is a vocative, and “man” is just a phrase that is there to amplify the meaning. However, Frank’s usage of “boy” in this verse could be interpreted as both, and that means the love he’s talking about could be male or female. Note that when “Thinkin Bout You” came out as a single it was still unknown if he was straight or not. Prior to the release of channel ORANGE, he came out as bisexual.

line: I was psycho and shit, I was writin’ on shit, I was ghost-writing
vault_lines: I was psycho and shit, I was writin' on shit, I was ghost-writing
meaning:
After Hurricane Katrina devastated the Southeastern United States in late August 2005, Ocean’s dormitory and studio were flooded, raided, and looted forcing him to move to Los Angeles in search of opportunities as a songwriter and musician. During this era of his career, without formal connections to the industry, Ocean found work as a ghostwriter, eventually earning songwriter credits on major artists' songs, like John Legend’s “Quickly,” Justin Bieber’s “Bigger,” and even Beyoncé’s “I Miss You.”

Ocean described in an interview with Passionweiss:

I’d work every day sometimes two sessions a day, 16-18 hr days. A lot of the songs never left my hard drive. I’d work for the sake of working. Sometimes so and so would hear something and they’d come in and work with me.

This sense of anonymity and mindless work as a ghostwriter reflects the sentiment of shock when he was eventually offered a contract by Def Jam, a deal that has since become infamous.

Ocean’s first love would not reveal his feelings for him until three years after Ocean confided in him:

line: There’s a bull and a matador dueling in the sky

meaning:
The constellations Orion (the hunter, or “matador”) and Taurus (the “bull”) can be seen dueling in the Northern Hemisphere’s winter sky.









Only one (the bull or matador) can survive and the loser falls from heaven. Animals are generally considered to lack moral sense, so this is not a mere instance of Manichean’s good and evil: there is no “correct” decision, no morally acceptable side to align himself with. Still, smoking weed elevates Frank to heaven, but he’ll eventually come down from his high. As such, he is in limbo, teetering in his appraisal of the situation, unsure if he should take Auntie Rosie’s advice or inhale for a temporary ride to heaven, or at least a temporary absence from his feelings & loneliness.

meaning:
The common themes in “Solo” as well as “Solo (Reprise)” are feeling alone when facing life’s problems and inevitably falling to low points in one’s life.

The word “solo” represents both of these themes in a clever double entendre, referring to “going solo” as struggling to face these troubles by himself, or  “going solo/so low” at this point in his life by resorting to drugs and ignoring his mother’s advice to keep his problems at bay.

Also, the arrangement for this song is just Frank and an organ, as if he was playing a solo or just reminds you of the “solo” organ.

line: Now stay away from highways My eyes like them red lights Right now, I prefer yellow Redbone, so mellow Fuck ‘round, be cuttin’ you Think we were better off solo
vault_lines: My eyes like them red lights
meaning:
“Yellow” and" redbone" are slang for a light-skinned black person and “cutting” means sex.

While “highways” and “red lights” refer to drug use—something Frank’s aunt warns against on “Be Yourself,” they may also refer to the fast-paced lifestyle that often accompanies fame. Red eyes are a common side effect of smoking marijuana and/or lack of sleep.

Yellow lights tend to indicate slowing down or using caution on the road. Similarly, Frank uses the yellow light metaphor to express that right now, he just wants to take things slow.

The use of yellow is also likely a reference to his sexuality. Knowing that the blond/blonde theme, is a metaphor for Frank’s bisexuality, he is technically in-between being gay and straight, similar to how a yellow light is in-between red and green.

Connecting this phrase to the previous, Frank gives us a sort of narrative. After confessing his feelings outside the party, Frank and this person begin a relationship. Frank can’t handle being in a relationship because of his drug use and lust, so he ends up fucking around (cheating) on them. Ultimately, in a sad echo of his proclamation at the end of the previous phrase, Frank breaks things off, saying they were better off solo.

line: It’s Hell on Earth, and the city’s on fire Inhale, in Hell, there’s Heaven
vault_lines: It's Hell on Earth, and the city's on fire
meaning:
Frank is commenting on the current tumultuous and chaotic state of the world. When he smokes, he reaches “heaven,” a happier place that is free of everyday problems.

“Inhale” is a play on “in hell,” which is ironic considering the weed’s feelings of “heaven.” Frank also juxtaposes getting high to opiate his feeling of “so low.”

Furthermore, this continues the theme of choosing between the traditional definitions of heaven and hell. Typically, smoking marijuana would be associated with Hell, but to Frank it is heaven. Within the traditional concept of “Hell” lies Frank’s “Heaven.” Another example in Frank’s music of duality would be his frequently addressing his own bisexuality.

Frank could also be discussing the inherent duality of life. That things are seldom so cut and dry that anything is purely evil or purely good. Even in the worst situations there is good, even “in hell there’s heaven”.

“Akh” is Arabic for “brother” and “akhi” is Arabic for “my brother”; this has several interpretations:

Not to criticize people haphazardly.

What goes around comes around.

line: It begins to blur, we get older (Blur) Summer’s not as long as it used to be Every day counts like crazy (Smoke, haze, wait)
vault_lines: Solstice ain't as far as it used to be
meaning:
Expressing a very common sentiment amongst people as they age, namely that time seems to go by faster the older you get.

As a kid everyone can probably remember their summer vacations from school seeming to be almost endless, but as you grow the summer, and often entire years, seem to fly by in the blink of an eye.

There is a lot of thought and study that has gone into this phenomenon. One idea is that, when you’re younger, you experience more “first’s” in your life, and this higher concentration of new experiences makes this time more memorable and seem more significant in hindsight.

Another is the simple fact that, as you get older, each passing year represents a smaller proportion of your cumulative time on earth so far and, as such, feels shorter and less significant.

Regardless of the reasons though, the message is clear. Life is short and time flies, so enjoy every day. Carpe Diem!

Frank plays with his words here, creating a new but related image with each line.

“On comes the evening” refers very obviously to the sunset. “Gold seeking ends” plays off this sunset imagery—the golden light of the sunset signals the end of the day, but it also evokes the “nothing gold can stay” mentality that perfuses the majority of Blonde. Gold also flows into the next line of “piece in my hands,” creating ‘gold piece’—a valuable watch or piece of jewelry that is worth more than the “gold-seeking” friends who are hustling and possibly coveting his success.

The line also references the classic saying “a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush,” which means it’s better to stick with what you have than to risk for the unknown. The “piece” in Frank’s hand may be a joint he’s holding, which is helping him to reach his inner “peace.” This peace brought by the high is worth the same as a “gold piece” and is worth more than a friend.

The final line about “limbs over shoulder” bring the verse back around to earlier subject of the song, love-making, with the knees of his lover hooked over his shoulders. It could also refer to his partner’s arms in an embrace. The “piece/peace” could then also refer to the lover, whose physical brand of comfort is worth twice what a mere friend might offer with their words and support.

These lines in the final verse  show that what Frank is really reaching for throughout this smokey, sex-drenched song is the inner peace that these activities bring along with the rush of dopamine.

meaning:
Although commonly misquoted as “Bet we sell the tickets out next week; on me, on my partners,” an accurate transcription of the line appears in the lyric sheets accompanying the 2017 LP reissue of Frank Ocean’s Endless:

Bet we sell the bickets out next week
On me, on my bodness

“Bickets” is possibly a portmanteau of “big-ticket,” suggesting he anticipates his album & shows will attract large audiences, making them big-ticket items. The mention of “next week” could allude to the album Blonde, released a day after Endless. The phrase “On me, on my bodness” appears to be an emphatic expression, a confident assertion that he will attain success through his strength & determination (akin to the idiomatic phrases “on my life” or “over my dead body”). Moreover, “bickets” and “bodness” act as an alliteration, which closes the verse with a rhythmic pattern.

Alternatively, within the context of the previous lines, Ocean could be referencing his contribution to Kanye West’s The Life of Pablo, with the mention of sitting in the audience at “The Garden,” referencing the album premiere he attended in February 2016 at Madison Square Garden; the lines may be an expression of his desire to emulate a similar experience for himself.

line: [Chorus: Frank Ocean]
vault_lines: Poolside convo about your summer last night (Ooh, yeah)
meaning:
Frank Ocean sings the first chorus in “Self Control” with a similar high-pitched vocal effect (+8 semitones) heard in the song’s introduction (+4 semitones), evoking a younger version of himself. Slow Hollows singer Austin Feinstein leads the second chorus, supported by high-pitched vocals by Ocean.

Feinstein, who co-arranged track, identified himself as the deeper voice in “Self Control” in a 2016 Vice interview:

[Frank Ocean] actually wanted either a female vocalist or me to sing higher. I’m just not capable of anything like that, it would just sound horrible and forced… So I was like, “OK, rather than forcing something, I’m just going to do what I do, and if he hates it, then that’s fine. That’s just what I do.” And he actually liked it a lot.

Following the release of Blonde, many fans misidentified Feinstein for Swedish rapper Yung Lean. Those familiar either artists’ voice may find this strange; however, with the pre-release zeitgeist in mind, the source of the confusion is more apparent. Leading up to Boys Don’t Cry & Blonde, many fans were excited by reports of Lean working with Ocean on his upcoming album. Upon its release in August 2016, fans anxiously waiting to hear Lean on the record mistook Feinstein’s deep & soft vocal performance for the Swedish rapper, with the power of suggestion maximizing the similarities and minimizing the differences between their voices. News of this alleged feature then spread through online discussions, media outlets, and public databases, leading more fans to expect or associate Lean with “Self Control.” Official track credits for Blonde were not available immediately after its release, which could have clarified the matter. Some outlets later corrected the record after the album’s liner notes were included with the November 2016 Black Friday reissues. Apple Music briefly listed Lean as a vocalist for “Self Control” (oddly enough, as the track’s only performer) when it introduced song credits to the platform in 2023; although, this was later corrected, removing Lean entirely.

However, Yung Lean does appear on Blonde, only later in the penultimate track “Godspeed,” performing vocals in between the first & second verses.

Nevertheless, in Feinstein’s 2016 interview with Vice, he alluded to other vocal performances for “Self Control” that did not make the final cut:

[Frank Ocean] had a couple different versions of the song and a couple different people singing the same part. It never really came together right.

It’s possible a recording of Lean singing “Self Control” exists; however, in the released version, he is neither a primary vocalist, a discernible background vocalist, nor listed in the official album credits, despite some online databases listing erroneous credits derived from unofficial sources.

He dreams within a dream, feels within a seam of thinking between the lines as  Sartre and Philip K. Dick might; trying to find a thought within a thought: between drugs and misunderstandings.

He’s getting lost in his thoughts hoping he could see God. He thinks of a dreamer who could think of dreaming and gets a glimmer of God. Frank thinks of a hopeful guy, who in his hopefulness and faith gets a glimmer of God. But then when Frank tries to get the glimmer of God, within his own thoughts and efforts, he cannot. The glimmer of God, like nirvana, is as rare as the feathers from a phoenix.

Less spiritually speaking and more philosophically: this also fits in with the theory of reflexivity: “the movement whereby that which has been used to generate a system is made, through a changed perspective, to become part of the system it generates” (Hayles, How we Became Posthuman, page 43). Similarly, Jorge Luis Borges' story, “The Circular Ruins,” in which Borges “imagines a narrator who creates a student through his dreaming only to discover that he himself is being dreamed by another” (43) details a similar line of philosophical thinking that is trapped in reflexivity, which appears critical to Frank’s lyrics here.

His ideas of conforming to societal expectations and starting a family are reminiscent of 1950s America after World War 2, which saw millions of Americans move out to the suburbs and inspired a baby boom. And you protest and you picket sign

Frank could also be speaking about his struggles being a queer man who feels pressure from society to settle down with a woman, ignoring that he has interests in men as well. By “living outside,” Frank suggests he will escape those social pressures and live his life as he chooses.

He continues the directional metaphors with this “loop”, which harkens back to the cyclical nature of life touched on in “Nights”:

Depression can tend to be cyclical (or “recurrent”) as well. It is expressed here as a recurrent “hell” that Frank has experienced and ostensibly can’t escape, given the fact that a loop is, by definition, self-enclosed.

line: I can’t relate to my peers I’d rather live outside I’d rather chip my pride than lose my mind out here
vault_lines: I'd rather go to jail
meaning:
After making a possible reference to a male lover, the song retreats from that failed romance to Frank’s problems with intimacy in general. Frank’s unique idiosyncrasies—and possibly his struggles with his sexuality—make it hard to him to fit himself into mainstream society. “I can’t relate to my peers” could then relate to feeling alienated for having such a different view on love than other famous male artists in the game.

Moreover, despite refusing to categorize his sexuality, his love affairs with men have captured the public’s interest and he has become well-known as an “LGBTQ artist.” LGBTQ artists find themselves under a tremendous amount of pressure to be a “model” minority—to speak for the whole of their demographic. Since Frank prefers not to be labeled, he might not feel like he can relate to the LGBTQ community, and feels alienated from queer circles as well as from mainstream society.

“I’d rather chip my pride than lose my mind out here” then becomes a retreat from his fanbase’s rabid curiosity about him and the unearned veneration he’s gotten as a “queer icon.”

Frank sees himself going crazy if he follows the same path as his peers. He doesn’t mind being seen as “weak,” he just wants to be happy with who he is.

With these lines, Frank comes to the heart of his insecurities relating to his fame and his issues with intimacy. Oftentimes when someone comes out they get empty platitudes about how they are “so brave.” However, being brave is not the same as being honest, as trying to exist as yourself in the world. In fact, calling someone brave for disclosing a part of their identity functionally reduces them to the struggle of being that thing, focusing on its negative aspects, and not on offering support or acceptance. Calling someone “brave” also puts pressure on them to “stay strong,” to muffle their own misgivings, doubts, and fears because they are “setting an example” for others.

Frank interpolates Elliott Smith’s song “A Fond Farewell”—the track appears on Smith’s posthumous 2004 album From a Basement on the Hill. The protagonist in Smith’s song tries but fails to conquer drug addiction and instead, he retreats to one last hit of heroin—a fond farewell to a friend.

After a long battle with substance abuse and an ongoing struggle with depression, Elliott Smith passed away in his Los Angeles home in 2003. Frank has a preoccupation with suicide that pops up in his songs repeatedly.

But here, these lyrics highlight Frank’s discomfort with society; namely, how it evolved without his consent and how he became entangled in its superficial qualities. He bids goodbye to who he once was—knowing that he cannot disassociate his present self from his past—and dares to be brave and transgress contemporary values that he disagrees with.

meaning:
Frank’s relationship with ‘pop’ is complicated. Ocean entered the game writing for Justin Bieber and John Legend, soon penning his own radio-friendly tunes like “Swim Good” or “Novacane”. The tracks caught the ears of Kanye and Beyoncé, opening Ocean’s door to making mainstream pop music for a larger pool of listeners. Released one year later, “Thinkin Bout You” may be Frank’s most perfect pop song. The track cracked the Billboard top 40 and has since become a mainstream favourite.

Despite this past spotlight, 2017 Frank notes that he’s surprised at his own success and the success of those that imitate him (as referenced in the previous line).

He notes that he cockblocks himself with ‘pop’, most likely referring to evasive behaviour and an independent status as a recording artist. Frank’s got anti-industry beef with everyone from the Grammys to Def Jam, but has recently found time for crossover hits like “Slide” and “RAF”. He could also be referring to his experimental direction on records like Endless and Blonde. Unlike channel ORANGE, the records don’t have much in the way of a mainstream pop sound, being more akin to the ‘experimental pop’ of cited influence The Beach Boys. General Song Overview:

“Pyramids” contains two distinct stories told from different perspectives, which take place in two different time periods (namely ancient Egypt and modern day America). The stories are connected by similar story elements, themes, and the Cleopatra motif.



The first part of the story is told by an Egyptian Pharaoh, whose Queen – the historically famous Egyptian ruler Cleopatra – has been reportedly kidnapped. As a response sends out all his powerful forces to get her back.

The first verse likely sees this ruler envisioning a great and powerful future with his strong black Queen – this thought may have occurred before or after Cleopatra went missing.

In the next verse the King has discovered that Cleopatra wasn’t taken against her will – she betrayed their kingdom and ran off with another man. This betrayal marks then end of Cleopatra’s life and of their once-powerful kingdom.

The present-day story then begins (along with a change in the beat), with a man awaking (this may imply that the first part of the song was a dream or at least that we are now in a new day).

He describes waking up to your girl, which connects him with the Cleopatra-stealing man of the first story. The way he describes the girl suggests that the Pyramid she’s working at tonight is a strip club or some kind of prostitution den.

He then describes his life, which shows him as a moderately successful pimp; Cleopatra is presumably one of his “workers”.

The present-day storyline then continues – but is told from the perspective of a pitiful man who has hired a prostitute. She makes him feel wanted, though he’s an unemployed loser that has to pay for her services. The final line of his story implies that they had a relationship previously, where she actually loved him and he didn’t have to pay for it – connecting him with the cuckolded man of the Ancient Egypt story.

The entire song as a whole spins a rich and complex web of imagery and motif that touches on many topics and themes. Among the most prevalent are betrayal, infidelity, exploitation, and loss of dignity.

It is likely that Frank is exploring the fall of African-American people – from powerful black Kings and Queens to lowly pimps and hookers – through exploitation (by society, the “white man”, etc.), and their own doing.

Frank raps about taking drugs and what they do to his brain, linking in to ‘brain on drugs’ in the following line.

The smoking is related to marijuana, a drug he references in other songs. The drinking could be a reference to alcohol but Frank seems to clarify that it’s in fact lean as he is using a styrofoam cup – a container popular amongst rappers for drinking lean. Both of these drugs are popular for their relaxing effect, tying into Frank’s attempt to find peace of mind and relax.

The stream of consciousness connects the white of the cup to the white of eggshells as Frank delves into some nice imagery:

• Firstly making a play on words on the popular phrase ‘you can’t make an omelette without breaking eggs’. The ‘omelette’ is a metaphor for his brain and the eggshells are the negative effects of the drugs on his mental state. Frank takes drugs to relax and gain peace of mind but the health defects of drugs – perhaps paranoia – are preventing Frank from achieving his desired state.
• Frank tried to make an omelette (gain peace of mind) but a drug-free route would have been better, connecting to the song’s theme of “Purity.”
• His earlobes being yellow furthers the omelette/brain analogy as the egg yolks are spilling out his head like the effects of drugs are coming out of him. The yellow earlobes could be a reference to him wearing jewellery – gold earrings.
• The use of eggs as an analogy links into common phrases related to taking drugs like ‘frying one’s brain’ and someone’s mind being ‘scrambled’.

line: The call had dropped when the FaceTime paused
vault_lines: The call had dropped when the FaceTime paused
meaning:
Rocky prefers to avoid phone calls because they feel disconnected and distant–he instead likes face to face interaction, as it is much more personal. Rocky has mentioned his dislike towards FaceTime in the past on “Blowin' Minds (Skateboard)”:

I don’t waste time on the FaceTime

line: I’ve been busy (Busy, bitch) I’ve been fuckin’ busy, I’ve been busy fuckin’ I’ve been all kinds of busy, or sorta kinda busy Like shorty, is we fucking? Well if not, then fuck it Apologies to the fam, we thought we ducked ’em Said ”I was in a rush”, but I was busy rushin’ It’s busy shit, busy that (Busy this), busy this (Uh), and I need a minute (Hold on)
vault_lines: I've been busy (Busy, bitch)
meaning:
Despite having dropped his first studio album since his 2015 AT.LONG.LAST.A$AP, Rocky has been working hard. In the 3 years since, he has kept busy with two volumes of an A$AP Mob compilation–Cozy Tapes, Vol. 1:Friends and Cozy Tapes, Vol. 2: Too Cozy–and a handful of choice features, including G-Eazy’s hit track “No Limit”. In a 2017 interview with GQ, Rocky said that he has been working to expand his musical potential:

My new album is really about testing new sounds. I don’t just rap—I actually make music. That’s why it takes time.

Rocky also mentioned the fact he has been rushing to drop the project:

When do you want to put the album out?

ASAP—no pun intended.

On top of that, A$AP Rocky has had the duties that come with being the rap game’s preeminent, fashion-forward trendsetter. In 2016, he was notably revealed as a face of Dior Homme.

line: I’ll smack a bitch like it’s hot hands
vault_lines: I'll smack a bitch like it's hot hands
meaning:
“Hot hands” is a children’s game which can be played by two players. The object of the game is for a person to slap the back of the other person’s hands before A can pull them away.

The reference is a display of Frank’s ruthlessness, as he is unhesitant to smack any oppostion.

The line may also reference a fight that Ocean had with Chris Brown back in 2013.

line: Spendin’ time, spinnin’ out toward a desire that wasn’t pure
vault_lines: Spendin' time, spinnin' out toward a desire that wasn't pure
meaning:
Ocean is reminiscing on a time where he would partake in jobs that he did not find desirable. As he recalled: “Oh man I had numerous hustles … Washing cars was one of them, and mowing lawns and walking dogs.” He even touched upon this before on “Futura Free” where he sings:

I ain’t had me a job since 2009
   I ain’t on no sales floor

After, Hurricane Katrina hit Ocean’s hometown of New Orleans he moved to Los Angeles  to develop his music career after establishing contact with people in the music industry.

It took Frank a bit more time to become successful, starting with his 2011 mixtape nostalgia, ULTRA, but in 2009 he was able to stop having a “day job” and focus on his musical career in earnest. Thus from then on he didn’t need to worry about financial needs as much, and could spend more time focusing on ensuring he created top quality music.

Ocean also spoke about the purity of his music-making in an interview back in 2013 with Oyster Magazine:

Well, my attitude was pure. I love to make music, and I love to write. It was writing first. I love to write and express myself in that medium, so that was the pure part — just the love of doing something.



Ocean’s early music days

line: Read my mind, free’d my mind, feed my mind, makes sense Just like mirrors on the wall, just like sittin’ on me
vault_lines: Read my mind, free'd my mind, feed my mind, makes sense
meaning:
Frank is recalling that these things like dance crazes and Nas’s music were eye-opening to him. They “read his mind” in a sense, and gave him freedom, especially in thought, and probably in self-expression.

They made things “make sense” to him as if he were looking into a mirror the whole time. He needed these things to realize who he was.

This line also interpolates a section of the sampled song, “I Gotta Find Peace of Mind” by Lauryn Hill, where the bridge begins

Cuz anything’s possible, oh anything is possible
Please come free my mind, please come meet my mind
Can you see my mind, oh
Won’t you come free my mind?
Oh I know it’s possible

line: Chewing on nothing (Yeah) You’re tweakin’ or somethin’, you’re reachin’ for somethin’ You’re speakin’, speak up then, you’re thinkin’, you’re overthinkin’
vault_lines: chewing on nothing (Yeah)
meaning:
These few lines are meant to reflect some of the negatives of drug use, which is a theme in this verse.

There is a muffled voice behind these lines, symbolizing the feeling of disconnect and distance that a user gets when under the influence of drugs.

The lines themselves describe the lack of control and inhibition that a drug user experiences. This is done through Frank telling the user what they’re doing, implying that they aren’t aware of their actions. This also describes the paranoia experienced by some drug users, and could be an internal monologue of Frank’s encounter with this paranoia.

Although Frank sometimes mentions drug use casually and portrays it in a positive light, throughout this verse he highlights the unfavorable aspects of it, and denounces the drugs that have recently become ‘cool’ to be addicted to:

Comfortable low nigga, fuck Xans
Salt on a slug, soda (lean) on slugged teeth

line: Nigga, pour up soda, nigga, hold that cough
vault_lines: Nigga, pour up soda, nigga, hold that cough
meaning:
Soda or any carbonated beverage is typically mixed with promethazine/codeine cough syrup to produce the narcotic, lean. However, Rocky chooses to remove the addictive part of the concoction in order to find his “natural” peace of mind without any chemical alterations.

This is quite shocking since lean is Rocky’s drug of choice as seen throughout his discography; for example, he once created an ode to the narcotic titled “Fine Whine”.

line: Fast forward, linings on my skull (This what that voice in your head says when you try to get piece of mind) This the type of design I could afford
vault_lines: Fast forward, linings on my skull (This what that voice in your head says when you try to get piece of mind)
meaning:
Linings on his skull could be referring to a popular hairstyle amongst African-Americans; waves.
Waves are usually acquired by wearing du-rags, which are generally inexpensive. Ocean has sung about his waves previously, on “Ivy”:

No matter what I did
My waves wouldn’t dip back then



Frank is also referring to getting designs shaved into your head, which was popular back in the late 2000s. Because of his financial situation at the time, he could only afford to get lined up, and not have exaggerated designs put in.

line: Salt on a slug, soda on slugged teeth,
vault_lines: Salt on a slug, soda on slugged teeth,
meaning:
Another example of Ocean’s clever word play.

When a slug comes in contact with salt, its moist skin loses all of its water and it dies quickly. Ocean uses this as a metaphor for for the effect of the narcotics on his brain.

To be “slugged up” is to have a mouth accessorized with gold and other precious metals. Soda most likely refers to the previously mentioned lean, which has the effect of making him move in a slowed demeanor, like a slug.

line: Comfortable slow, who the fuck ran?
vault_lines: Comfortable slow, who the fuck ran?
meaning:
When one takes drugs, they often describe it as a ‘rush’. When sober, things could be described as much slower as you do not have a rush to either have fun or to help you cope with stress.

Similar to the line above, Frank states again that he does not not need this rush since he is comfortable being sober, or in this case, slow.

The line is also probably referring to the fact Frank took his time to release both Blonde and Endless, despite the pressure to be faster. Frank felt more comfortable perfecting his art rather than rushing to release it.

After the album’s release Frank wrote on his Tumblr:

Thank you all. Especially those of you who never let me forget I had to finish. Which is basically everyone of y'all. Haha. Love you

line: Rewind dance crazes
vault_lines: I've been busy (Busy, bitch)
meaning:
Frank is calling back to the short life of Internet-age dances (often referred to as novelty and fad dances) that usually don’t last more than a month or two.

The specific mention of dancing may be a deeper metaphor for joy, and rewinding to them would mean that said joyful memories are long gone and, which is a common theme across Frank’s discography, especially with his mixtape Nostalgia, Ultra., where tracks like Strawberry Swing talk about this specific topic in detail.

line: Amphetamines for the dosage, keepin’ me up and focused
vault_lines: Amphetamines for the dosage, keepin' me up and focused
meaning:
Amphetamine is a central nervous system stimulant that affects chemicals in the brain and nerves that contribute to hyperactivity and impulse control.

Amphetamine is the active ingredient in Adderall which is used to treat attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). Adderall is an extremely common prescription drug abused by college and high school kids as it allows users to stay awake for prolonged periods of time and helps the brain to focus.

Rocky uses the drug to get in his bag while making this album. Studio hours often encompass shifts lasting multiple hours. As he has stated on this album previously it was hard for him to work on the album as he was focusing on fashion as well as other things.

line: Born before the virus was cured,
vault_lines: Born before the virus was cured,
meaning:
The “virus” refers to addiction, which is the theme of this song. There is not cure for it yet.

‘The virus’ can also allude to the HIV/AIDS virus: Frank is an open bisexual, and ‘Black/African American gay and bisexual men’ account for the largest number of diagnoses for HIV; potentially a worrying fact for the artist.

Frank was born in 1987. It was in 1981 that the AIDS virus was first clinically observed; the first antiretroviral drug was approved in 1987.

Frank has previously discussed his ‘troubling obsession with unprotected sex’ on his 2012 ‘Sierra Leone’. Lyrics read:

I just ran outta Trojans

line: Brain on drugs, I still ain’t got no peace of mind, fuck
vault_lines: Brain on drugs, I still ain't got no peace of mind, fuck
meaning:
Most people take drugs to escape from the stress of everyday life, for example when a person smokes marijuana, dopamine and other chemicals are released by the brain, creating a sense of calm and well-being.

Notice the juxtaposition created with his lack of peace of mind, and the lyrics in the hook. In essence, Ocean uses the drugs as an escape. Previous lyrics of his has shown his use and experimentation with such as in “Solo”:

Gone off tabs of that acid

Frank may also be referencing a 1980s advertisement best known for its tagline, “This is your brain on drugs” in conjunction with his prior mention of eggs:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3FtNm9CgA6U

This line can also be a reference to “Call of da Wild”, by OutKast:
https://genius.com/821786

line: Two more drinks of everything before the bar closed Face-to-face with my demons at a barstool
vault_lines: Two more drinks of everything before the bar closed
meaning:
Drinking brings Rocky to face issues that he otherwise tries to avoid, a painful one is referenced in these lyrics, with a direct reference to his sister’s death in September 2016.

Rakim, originating from the dangerous neighborhoods of Harlem, has witnessed the death of many of his family members due to violence and drugs, his father in 2012, and his brother when he was only 13, who was killed.

A$AP Yams, a close friend and associate of Rocky who died as the result of a drug overdose, is also most likely one of the demons he mentions.

line: Can’t cope when your heart broke, soft-spoken, roll somethin’, cop somethin’, Narco
vault_lines: Can't cope when your heart broke, soft-spoken, roll somethin', cop somethin', Narco
meaning:
In these lines, Rocky brings up his difficulties of coping with heartbreak, and the different ways he tries to combat these feelings.

“Soft spoken” is most likely refering to him letting the pain out by bringing up his problems and speaking about them in his music, just like he is doing in this verse.

“Roll something” could be him talking about rolling a blunt, thus trying to stabilize his mood and emotions with marijuana.

“Copping” is slang for getting/ buying something, so Rocky is once again most likely talking about the usage of drugs. A “Narco” is someone that is involved in organized crime or drug dealing relating to narcotics. The most recent ties of this word in popular culture comes from Netflix’s hit series Narcos, which follows the life of drug kingpin Pablo Escobar.

line: Saint like Joan of Arc, bro
vault_lines: Saint like Joan of Arc, bro
meaning:
Joan of Arc was a French military leader during the Hundred Years' War and is considered a national heroine in her home country after her victories over the English at Orléans. She died a martyr’s death in the hands of the English and was burned at the stake at the age of 19. After her death, she was canonized as a Roman Catholic Saint.

Using the word “saint” to describe a person is often just a metaphor for leading a good life, but Rocky brings up a few more points by comparing himself to Joan of Arc; he indirectly states that he has made similar sacrifices for his hometown of Harlem, New York. Comparing himself to Joan of Arc might also refer to him being “burned at the stake,” considering how much he’s been criticized throughout his music career.

line: Freeway, no Rozay, brute force, Brüt champagne
vault_lines: Freeway, no Rozay, brute force, Brüt champagne
meaning:
“Freeway, no Rozay” simultaneously refers to rapper Rick Ross as well as “Freeway Rick”, born as Ricky Donnell Ross, who is a convicted drug trafficker active in the 1980s.

‘Rozay’ is a nickname for the American rapper Rick Ross, whose birth name is William Leonard Roberts II. The stage name is likely inspired by the drug dealer Ricky Ross, who filed a law suit against the rapper’s stage name asking for $10 million. Rozay won the court battle and could keep his stage name.

In this line, Frank also mentions Brut champagne, a dry sort of the French sparkling wine from the Champagne region. Since Rozay is a homonym of Rosé (French for ‘pink’), Frank refers to Rosé Brut Champagne, which comes from a blend of red and white wine.

line: Months past and months in between since me and my sister would speak, not a call or visit in weeks Lost nothin’ since September, last seen her September ’16 Man, it feels like...
vault_lines: Months past and months in between since me and my sister would speak, not a call or visit in weeks
meaning: Rocky’s sister Erika B. Mayers passed away in September 2016 following a drug overdose around the release of the A$AP Mob’s Cozy Tapes, Vol. 1. Rocky and Erika were very close and her death deeply affected him. He opened up about her death in a 2018 interview with Complex.

line: See this what that voice in your head says when you try to get peace of mind “I gotta find peace of mind”
vault_lines: Fast forward, linings on my skull (This what that voice in your head says when you try to get piece of mind)
meaning:
This is a sample of Ms. Lauryn Hill’s “I Gotta Find Peace of Mind” off “MTV Unplugged 2.0”



Rocky uses this as the chorus to underly the theme of both his and Frank’s search for a peace of mind. Through all the adversity both of them may face, as do all of us, it is important for us to find peace and purity in thought for the sake of ourselves and others.

This chorus also points out a certain irony. The frustration you feel when you don’t get peace of mind only makes the situation worse.  Ironically, the voice in your head tells you to find peace of mind, but peace of mind can only be acquired if the voice in your head is silenced.

line: Roof lost on the Wraith, roof lost on the way
vault_lines: Roof lost on the Wraith, roof lost on the way
meaning:
“Wraith” refers to the 2018 Rolls-Royce Wraith, the latest model from the British luxury automobile maker frequently referenced by rappers in songs.



Frank is talking about driving with the top down on the freeway, aimlessly with little direction.

line: Lose someone every release, it feels like the curse is in me (A$AP) Press is gone and I grief
vault_lines: Man, it feels like...
meaning:
This is a personal reference that has been noted by fans and Rocky himself which others and him seem to notice that after every release of his albums a loved one or close person dies. For instance, with LONG.LIVE.A$AP, his dad died only months later in 2012.

With the release of AT.LONG.LAST.A$AP in 2015, his dearest friend and member A$AP YAM$ died of an overdose before the album was released.

A month after the release of Cozy Tapes, Vol. 2: Too Cozy his sister also died in an overdose in a similar fashion to Yams.

Rocky goes into further detail of this in his interview  with Genius.

With the release of TESTING this “curse” may have been passed to A$AP Press who was close with fellow members of the Mob.

line: Reserved in the Mercer for two years in two suites, took out the bed like it’s fuck sleep
vault_lines: Reserved in the Mercer for two years in two suites, took out the bed like it's fuck sleep
meaning:
The Mercer is a luxury hotel in the heart of NYC’s SoHo neighborhood, and is known for hosting high-end clientele. It’s also the location in which Frank Ocean recorded a large portion of his visual album, Endless and likely, Blonde.

Frank is notorious for staying in hotels for extended periods of time, and coupled with the fact that he purchased an apartment in NYC, it refers to a time when Frank was in between housing.



Frank also mentions his hotel stints on his 2016 track “Sideways” from his conceptual visual album Endless with the line

All this hotel living
Might as well pay the mortgage what I’m spending

Him taking out the beds refers to his hard work ethic while working on the albums. Colleagues who worked with Frank have also stated he has nocturnal habits of recording most of his songs.

“Fuck sleep” might refer to “Fukk Sleep," the fourth track on TESTING.

line: I rewind, Nas track 6,
vault_lines: I rewind, Nas track 6,
meaning:
Nas is a rapper from Queens, New York, who is often regarded as one of the all-time great MCs.



Frank is referring to the sixth track on Nas’s album Stillmatic, “Rewind”. Alternatively, he may be alluding to the sixth song on Illmatic, which is titled “Memory Lane (Sittin' in da Park)”.

Both of these joints from Nas harbor themes of memorialization, nostalgia and reminiscing — these elements are relevant to Frank’s verse as he spends time looking back on how things used to be. Ocean has often reflected on his past in his own work, such as on his debut mixtape nostalgia, ULTRA. and on “Ivy”:

You ain’t a kid no more
We’ll never be those kids again
It’s not the same, ivory’s illegal
Don’t you remember?

line: Fired the label like fuck brands
vault_lines: Fired the label like fuck brands
meaning: After the release of his visual album Endless, Frank was finally able to leave his contract with record label Def Jam Recordings and release his highly anticipated sophomore album Blonde under his own independent label, Boys Don’t Cry/Blonded. Frank described his prolonged fall out with Def Jam as a “seven-year chess game.”

line: Fast forward, bands out, got they hands out like they acknowledgin’ the Führer
vault_lines: Fast forward, bands out, got they hands out like they acknowledgin' the Führer
meaning:
With this line, Frank uses imagery of the Nazi party’s salute to their führer or leader, Adolf Hitler. The Nazi salute is done by extending the right arm out, with an open palm facing down, towards their flag and/or leader.



Frank is saying the people around him are looking for handouts now that he is rich and famous, with their hands out in a gesture asking for money when Frank feels he owes them nothing. This could also be viewed by Frank as him having power over them further contributing to the idea that he is their ruthless dictator the Führer.

line: Comfortable low nigga, fuck Xans
vault_lines: Comfortable low nigga, fuck Xans
meaning:
Frank is notorious for keeping a low profile, whether its his lack of social media (aside from his Tumblr account) or keeping quiet for over 4 years between releasing Channel Orange and Blonde.

Xanax is a pharmaceutical grade prescription drug that eliminates the feeling for needing anything else, it numbs you and makes you feel comfortable.



Xans have proven to be problematic with the recent wave of rappers, namely with the overdose of Lil Peep. Frank asserts that he gets just as much comfort in being alone in comparison to be taking Xanax to do so – he doesn’t need them to reciprocate the feeling.



In recent times, many of Frank’s peers within hip-hop have decided to stop using Xanax and other drugs:

https://twitter.com/smokepurpp/status/947648149241368576?lang=en

line: Can’t show my face if you spit for me (Spit for me, yeah)
vault_lines: Can't show my face if you spit for me (Spit for me, yeah)
meaning:
These two bars speak on the two sides of masculinity. Frank can’t “show [his] face” nor be around those who talk down when he is brought up in conversation. Usually, spitting on someone is interpreted as a sign of disrespect. Thus, this action is met with the cold touch of ignoring those that do so.

Ironically, “spit for me, yeah” is heard in a sexual tone as if it is perfect contradiction with the previous aggressive bar towards the notion of “spit”.

line: I’m the only one out here on the night loops I’m the only one out here on the night loops
vault_lines: I'm the only one out here on the night loops
meaning:
Frank may be reminiscing about driving or “looping” around the long, winding highways of California at night. Although their quite busy during the day, he’s the only car out on the roads when the sun goes down. He previously expressed his love for highways on “Solo”:

Now stay away from highways
My eyes like them red lights
Right now I prefer yellow
Redbone, so mellow

This may also reference Frank’s work ethic when producing “Provider,” a boom-bap, contemplative drum loop that Frank probably produced late at night when no one is in the studio. Alternatively, this line connects to how people struggle and working nights for their family. Frank states that he has been in that situation himself, in the sense how he had been working in the studio through the night, working on and shaping his songs.

line: Watch friend’s GoPro through fisheye lens, drownin’ off clear I just saw Jaws, divin’ under influence
vault_lines: Watch friend's GoPro through fisheye lens, drownin' off clear
meaning:
A GoPro is a video camera with a fisheye lens that is often used to film action sports. Its founder originally created it to take videos while surfing in the ocean. Jaws may refer to the 1975 Steven Spielberg-directed thriller about a man-eating shark or pro skater Aaron Homoki, whose nickname is “Jaws"—many of Frank’s closest friends are skaters.

The ocean water is clear, but “clear” also refers to clear liquor like vodka and gin—“drowning” is slang for being drunk, meaning “diving under the influence” is an allusion to drunk driving.

Frank has seen his friends' strong career beginnings, but he’s also seen them suffer from the trappings of success.

line: Chest pass, see mist off rotation (Swish, swisha)
vault_lines: Chest pass, see mist off rotation (Swish, swisha)
meaning:
In basketball, a chest pass is one that’s thrown straight from the torso with two hands. A good chest pass has a lot of spin on it, which Frank romanticizes by suggesting you might see “mist” coming off of it because of how fast it’s spinning.

Frank may be suggesting he is sharing smoke with his partner from by standing chest-to-chest with them and exhaling directly into his their mouth. This is also called a shotgun kiss.

The ad-lib plays off both interpretations, since “swish" is the sound a basketball makes when it goes through the net and “swisha” is slang for Swisher Sweets cigars.

line: New man comin’ up ahead on his own two
vault_lines: New man comin' up ahead on his own two
meaning:
“On his own two” is an abbreviation of the idiom “stand on your own two feet, which means accomplishing your goals on your own.

If this “new man” is a love interest, he may be Memo Guzman, since Frank mentioned him at the beginning of the verse.

line: Memo finna start actin’ out if I don’t see him soon Yeah my best friend ain’t backin’ out, it’s still on sight, fool
vault_lines: Memo finna start actin' out if I don't see him soon
meaning:
Memo Guzman was spotted with Frank at the Mayweather vs. McGregor fight on August 26, 2017, the night before “Provider” was released. Frank’s relationship with Memo was previously unknown, but it appears that they are close friends, possibly more. This would add an extra meaning to his line from 2016’s “Futura Free”:

You must ain’t get the memo
I don’t cut bitches no more



Memo tweeted “Provider” lyrics on July 7, far before the single’s release.

line: Sleepin’ on my belly in a loop like a serpent Talkin’ heads ripplin’ on the surface
vault_lines: Talkin' heads ripplin' on the surface
meaning:
“Loop like a serpent” is an allusion to the Ouroboros, an Ancient Egyptian symbol of a snake eating its own tail that represents cyclicality and the infinite cycle of life and death.

Talking Heads were an influential NYC-based indie band in the 1970s and ‘80s that helped spearhead the new wave movement. They’re also credited with revolutionizing looping and have been described as “human samplers.” Frank listed their track “Road to Nowhere” as one of his favorite songs in his Boys Don’t Cry ‘zine.

When dealing with this lover, Frank goes through a cycle that ends with him listening to music as he falls asleep alone because his lover will not grow up.



In a Tumblr post, Frank said he only sleeps on his stomach or his side to avoid lucid dreaming.

He also references the sleep issue(sleep paralysis)  in the song “Alabama”

Sleeping on my back, my body would wake up after me”

line: Been feelin’ like the Lord’s just out of reach for me (For me) How I feel lettin’ man speak How I feel lettin’ man speak for me (For me)
vault_lines: Been feelin' like the Lord's just out of reach for me (For me)
meaning:
Frank was raised Christian and seems to believe in God, but his romantic relationships with men complicate his faith. He explored the relationship between his faith and sexual identity on “Bad Religion” from 2012’s channel ORANGE. Frank left the pronoun in the line “I can never make him love me” vague enough that it works as a lamentation both that he could never win over a male lover and that, by trying to win his affections, he lost God’s love.

Frank has expressed fear that acts of God will tear him and a lover apart, so it seems as though he has consistently felt that God is judging him for his lifestyle. But he has also depicted God more beneficently on songs like “Biking” where he assures himself, “God gave you what you could handle”.

Here, “man” also alludes to mankind as a whole, because “man” is often used in the Bible to reference all of humanity. Frank may be suggesting that God’s commandments aren’t all-encompassing because everyone’s different.

line: You had you some birthdays, could you prove it? Show me the wisdom in your movement Show me some wisdom in your movement
vault_lines: You had you some birthdays, could you prove it?
meaning:
Frank has not seen this lover in a few years, and Frank is challenging them to show him what they have learned, sexually. As we grow older and experience new lovers, our own sexual prowess improves as we adopt techniques from our sexual escapades.

The chorus makes clear that Frank still has feelings for this person despite their recklessness. But unless the lover shows they have matured in their time away from Frank, Frank fears that their relationship will end for the same reason that it did when they were both younger.

line: Holyfield, keep your ears split for me
vault_lines: Holyfield, keep your ears split for me
meaning: Evander Holyfield is a boxer whose ear was infamously bitten off by Mike Tyson during their June 28, 1997 Heavyweight Championship match. Frank is asking his lover to keep their ears open for him in case he tries to contact them.

line: Pat the Patagonia pockets, tryna find my zip (Uh, where it’s at? Yeah)
vault_lines: Pat the Patagonia pockets, tryna find my zip (Uh, where it's at? Yeah)
meaning:
Patagonia is an American clothing company that sells designer outdoor clothing, like the jacket that Frank wore in the “Nikes” music video.



Frank puns on “zip” here—he’s searching for the zipper pocket on the front of his jacket where he is stashing a “zip,” which is slang for an ounce of weed. He could also be referring to a Zippo lighter.

Frank sang a similar line about stashing weed in his jacket on May 2017’s “RAF”:

Parka pocket full of mint leaves

line: Is you a natural blondie like Goku?
vault_lines: Is you a natural blondie like Goku?
meaning:
Goku is the protagonist of the Dragon Ball manga and television series. He usually has black hair, but when he changes into his natural Super Saiyan form, it turns blonde.

Blonde hair has been a major motif in Ocean’s lyrics since he named an album after it. On “Slide,” Frank presents dyeing hair blonde as an act of youthful carelessness. By asking his lover if they are a natural blonde, Frank is wondering whether or not they are as free spirited as he is.

The fact that Goku’s natural hair is black implies some irony in Frank’s question. As if he’s suggesting the person referenced is pretending to be something they’re not.

line: Since you been gone, I been having withdrawals
vault_lines: Since you been gone, I been having withdrawals
meaning:
Withdrawal is a symptom which comes when a previous user distances themselves from the drug they were addicted to. The effects of alcohol addiction typically result in extended seizures, and other withdrawal symptoms can incorporate depression and flu-like traits for cocaine and painkillers, respectively. André thus relates his lover to a drug, and by claiming that he was experiencing these symptoms, depicts their love as a type of high which 3000 now feels is unattainable. As with most recovering addicts, he wants to return to his old ways—as demonstrated by his reminiscing over their calls and intimacy later on the the verse—but in the outro 3000 takes a turn and hopes that his partner would just leave.

In addition, “withdrawals” acts as a double entendre for the coitus interruptus, or pull out method, used to prevent pregnancies—meaning that since the breakup between André and his lover, all of his intimate relationships have purely been out of lust with no further aspirations of having children together.

Kanye also expressed an idea similar to this when he rapped “Fat bitches swallowin, skinny bitches modelin.” Here Andre 3000 is saying that skinny girls are vapid and lack the emotional depth he’s looking for, they’re just arm candy who are good for show. Thick girls on the other hand “are made for cuddlin',” they’re not shallow (in the physical and emotional sense!) and are thus much more suited to real relationships. line: Sensei replied, ”What is your woman? Is she just a container for the child?”

A sensei is a teacher, someone who is there for guidance so you can make wiser choices.



Here, the Sensei asks Frank two questions that imply skepticism. They are questioning the importance of Frank’s female partner to him, the Sensei goes on to ask if she is nothing more than a vessel to carry Frank’s children.

The sensei doesn’t answer their own question, they simply ask Frank to re-evaluate his already inconclusive view of her. It is open for interpretation, not a concrete conclusion.

Frank could be using the Sensei character as a metaphor for his own conscience here. He continues to have an introspective conversation throughout the verses. He’s also making a rebuttal to the previous line. Your woman is more than just a container for a child, just like your brain is more than just a container for a mind.

Finally, the Sensei here is not given a gender – although stereotypically male, a Sensei can be of any gender, and the word Sensei is genderless in the Japanese language. This is rather fitting, as the Sensei here is the one helping Frank to open up about his feelings towards the different genders, as well as helping him understand himself.

Frank again references Hurricane Katrina and the flooding it caused, talking about how he witnessed people swimming in the flood waters, seemingly making the best out of the ungovernable. The “nose-dive” and “tall tower” create an exhilarating sense of climbing and jumping from a height. It was a moment in time where the world above was something to embrace, even though after that moment it’s all downhill from there.

Frank brings this back to the person he is singing about, the person who “showed him love,” creating another level of metaphor here for “diving in” to life, and to their relationship.

This may call back to an interview that Frank did with Wax Poetics back in 2012 in which he talked about experiencing floods during his childhood:

All the houses in New Orleans are raised off the ground because of floods and shit. So it was like three feet of water. My cousins and I stacked up milk crates and were using it as a diving board into the floodwaters. We were doing that all day until one of my neighbors came out there on a little swamp-style boat, and grabbed a water moccasin out of the water and cut its head off against the fence.

Similarly to the lines that open the verse, these lyrics are referenced in the “Godspeed” screenplay included in Frank’s Boys Don’t Cry magazine. At the end of Scene 1:

Steely looks down at his feet, and there’s ice on the grass though it’s simmer. Steely pulls his head up to say ‘snow’ but doesn’t even make the beginning sounds of the word. A single ball of alloy, white and coated with ice, spins around them like a tether ball to its poll. Shoobie still mouthing the words to a song playing in her head. ‘If you could fly then you’d feel south, up north’s gettin’ cold soon…The way it is we’re on land — still I’m someone to hold true'.

Feeling “south” is also a way to say that things haven’t gone well. For example, if something goes “south,” it is not going well. However, the line is a bit of a paradox (perhaps intentionally). Saying that if you could “fly,” then you would not be happy. Not feeling content with “flying” could emphasize the lack of control we have over anything, a theme of the verse.

This resolves the tension that has been created throughout the verses and hooks. The love that Frank’s spoken of, just like life, will inevitably end because that IS life. Shoobie: (Bobbing her head to music that isn’t playing, she sings) ‘That’s the way every day goes, every time we’ve no control…’

Color is a significant motif in Ocean’s music, from the title of his 2012 album channel ORANGE to symbolistic songs like “Eyes Like Sky” and “Pink Matter.” He also mentioned pink skies in “Sierra Leone.”

Here, Ocean expresses how we have no control over the color of the sky; it can be blue, or it can be pink and white.

The “black and yellow” ground calls to mind the image of black asphalt and yellow painted lines on a street.

These lines may also be connected to Hurricane Katrina, which Ocean alludes to in the second verse, in reference to an old proverb, “Red sky in the morning, sailors take warning.” Ocean is essentially using the notion that “we have no control” over the color of the sky as a way of coming to terms with what happened to New Orleans during Katrina.

Another interesting thing that links indirectly with this entire concept would be the story of Sarah Good, a woman accused of witchcraft in the Salem Witch Trials of 1692. Why does any of that matter? In Tyler’s acclaimed 2009 album Bastard, Tyler has a song called Sarah (whom he mentions on other occasions as well). Along with Raquel, Sarah and Salem all seem to represent different aspects of a similar girl Tyler (or any of his other personalities) has a clear obsession with.

Add that onto the new girl being introduced, Salem, and Tyler’s odd fascination with lakes and even killing women in them, and you discover a clear connection to the Salem Witch Trials of 1692 and the stories of WOLF, Bastard, and Goblin – perhaps Tyler is making a statement within his abstract, open-ended story of him and each of his endless personalities?

line: The Magna Carta

#THE MAGNA CARTA

Half the name of Jay-Z’s album Magna Carta Holy Grail. “Carta” is a play on “Carter,” Jay’s surname.

Historically, it’s called the Angevin charter, or  the Magna Carta, one of the first documents forced onto a King of England by a group of his subjects in an attempt to limit his powers by law and protect their privileges. It’s an essential document of history and the development of democracy.



Jay debuted the art for the album next to a page from the real Magna Carta in Salisbury, UK. “We are delighted that Jay Z has chosen Salisbury Cathedral, home to the finest of the four surviving original 1215 Magna Carta, as the location for the global premiere of his artwork for Magna Carta Holy Grail,“ The Dean of Salisbury, the Very Revd June Osborne, said.

We know how important Magna Carta, and all it represents, is to people across the globe. The ideals it embodies are still relevant today. Jay Z, through his album, is creating a huge awareness of this historic document and its modern significance to a huge audience in the run up to its 800th anniversary in 2015. We hope to welcome many of his fans here this summer to see the artwork in the Chapter House alongside our Magna Carta.

Jay also wants to draw attention to some of the deeper meanings of his lyrics through the Magna Carta Holy Grail album art, by drawing an inference to this quote:

I cross out words so you will see them more: the fact that they are obscured makes you want to read them
– JM Basquiat.

Pretty sweet for fans of history and hip-hop.

line: Elephant tusk on the bow of a sailing lady, docked on the Ivory Coast
vault_lines: Elephant tusk on the bow of a sailing lady, docked on the Ivory Coast
meaning:
These lines begin the usage of the white imagery portrayed throughout the song. Ivory is a color that’s an off-white. The image depicted is one in which a boat is docked in Cote d'Ivoire, a country known as the Ivory Coast.

The Ivory Coast has a long history with elephants and ivory  poaching. This country used to be filled with elephants, but currently, the population is under the threat of extinction due to poaching.

Elephants are poached for their ivory tusks, which are very valuable. The tusks being on the bow of a sailing lady (a ship) shows that they’ve already been killed. If you’d like to help stop elephant poaching, check out the Bloody Ivory website.



“Elephant tusks of the bore of a sailing lady docked on the Ivory Coast” might also refer to the slave trade and the money Europeans made off black bodies. The old money that helps them afford their Mercedes in a row, winding down the road…

These lines also bring to mind the Greek goddess Atalanta. Listen to how Frank pronounces “bow” like a bow and arrows, not like the bow of a ship. She has been depicted as carrying her arrows in an ivory quiver, and was, herself, a sailor. Her mythology involved sailing and the ocean. Numerous ships have been named Atalanta over the years, and of course, the city of Atlanta itself.



Another interpretation of these lines portray a reference to the ivory figureheads on slave ships (above), ornately decorated with the trappings of wealth, concealing squalor below deck. The comparison between “clean” white and “dirty” black takes on a new level of irony here, as it really the white slavers who are “dirty” in the figurative sense.

To tie it all back in to elephant poaching, note that these ships held cargo not only of human chattel, but also of ivory. When the wreck of the Dutch slaver Fredenborg was salvaged by divers, they found elephant ivory in the wreck. One can only imagine that the more readily dissolvable bones of slaves might also have been found.

line: On the holiday playin’ “Strange Fruit” If I’ma make it to a billi, I can’t take the same route
vault_lines: On the holiday playin' "Strange Fruit"
meaning:
This is a reference to Billie Holiday’s 1939 rendition of “Strange Fruit.” Famously sampled by Kanye West on 2013’s  “Blood on the Leaves,” the song provides a vivid description of lynching, and how it was rampant in The South. Note Jay’s usage of “holiday” and “billi,” as those words play along with the reference. Also note the homonyms ‘route’ and ‘root’; in “Strange Fruit,” Holiday says:

Southern trees bear a strange fruit
Blood on the leaves and blood at the root



The “holiday” in this line is most likely Independence Day, which also served as the release date for Magna Carta Holy Grail. To take the same route would be to die at the hands of discrimination. This is a continuation of the theme of expanding beyond what Jay has done in the past to accumulate wealth. In the beginning, he and Ty Ty sold drugs to make money; then he used rap to gain wealth; then he became an author, and so on.

Taking another approach at this line, the “route” could be in reference to transatlantic slave trade, a system notorious for the bringing of many slaves to colonial North America. The ships docked at ports in Africa, such as the Ivory Coast, and then went along their route to the colonies. This ties back in with the overall interpretation of the song that was first noted in the beginning of the chorus—that the ocean is symbolic in terms of enslavement, but also looked at as a sign of freedom.

As of 2013, Jay’s net worth was $500,000,000. He still had a long way to go in order to double his net worth. On June 3, 2019—nearly six years following the release of this song—Forbes reported that Jay had doubled his worth and officially become rap’s first billionaire.

line: Novocaine, Novocaine, Novocaine Novocaine, Novocaine (Oh) Numb the pain, numb the pain, numb the pain Numb the pain, numb the pain (Ah, oh) Novocaine, Novocaine, Novocaine (Ah) Novocaine, Novocaine (Oh) For the pain, for the pain (Oh, ooh-huh) Novocaine, Novocaine
vault_lines: Numb, numb, numb, numb
meaning:
A recent relationship was one of the inspirations for the album, as Frank Ocean revealed in a 2011 interview with Complex:

Going through heartbreak was new for me. […] I was just trying to make a record with the shit that I wanted to express. The shit that I wanted to get off my chest. […] A lot of this record is influenced by one relationship, but I don’t owe that whole project to one situation. It doesn’t matter what the details of it are.

The first heartbreak Frank is talking about is likely of him and his first love, who, as he detailed in his 2012 open letter, confessed his love to him in 2010, three years after they met, and which may also be the period in which their relationship fell apart, as Frank recounts in his 2016 song “Ivy,” in which he describes the gradual ruin of a past relationship after one revealed they loved the other. As Frank explained in an interview with the New York Times, he uses the different vocal pitches to sing as a different version of himself. Alongside with being a co-founder of the group, Yams was the co-owner of the group’s label, A$AP Worldwide.

Although he never had much of a stage presence, Yams was regarded as “hip-hop’s spirit guide” by the New York Times in 2013, and A$AP Rocky once exclaimed in a separate New York Times article sourced by Billboard that Yams was the “mastermind behind the scenes,” when speaking about the collective. On January 18, 2015, the A$AP Mob took to Twitter to confirm Yams' passing, stating:

Yams' passing was described as an “acute drug intoxication” according to the Chief Medical Examiner in an article published by DAZED. Several months later, on March 20, 2015, it was revealed to the public through a Rolling Stone Magazine article that Yams' passing was due to an accidental overdose of promethazine and codeine.

To “pour up” is to fill a cup or glass with a drink. The term has been used by artists such as Lil Wayne—specifically in his 2015 track “Pour Up”—when referring to the substance lean; an illegal narcotic drink, with its primary ingredients being promethazine and codeine. The line itself is inherently ironic, as Frank Ocean presumably pours up lean in order to celebrate the life of Yams—the very substance that killed him.

In 2016, an official music video for “Nikes” was released, which paid tribute to Yams by featuring A$AP Rocky carrying around a framed photograph of the late hip-hop mogul.



Pimp C was a legendary Texas hip-hop artist and producer who, along with Bun B, was a founding member of the iconic rap group UGK. He passed away in 2007 reportedly due to an accidental overdose from codeine-based cough syrup.

line: [Part I]
vault_lines: 'Round your city, 'round the clock
meaning:
Duality is a common motif that Frank Ocean employs throughout his discography, and the beat switch in “Nights” at 3:30 is a perfect example—it divides Blonde into two parts, placed at the 30-minute mark (30:03) of the 60-minute album (60:17). The instrumental build-up to the switch involves a chaotic arrangement of guitars, and the flip afterward introduces a more melancholic aura, known to cause goosebumps, as explored by Genius.

The theme of dualism materialized when Ocean released his independent magazine titled Boys Don’t Cry. Exploring the publication’s contents, two small lines of text appeared on the border of one page that simply read, “I GOT TWO VERSIONS. I GOT TWOOO VERSIONS…” Ocean also teased the line on April 7, 2015, through a Tumblr post.

A cropped picture of the page showing the text (Pitchfork, 2018).

Those who owned magazine copies also would stumble on a page that offers a different tracklist compared to the standard stream-able version. Further inspection revealed that there were two separate stylizations of the album’s title: streaming services such as Apple Music and Spotify list the album title as Blonde, while the cover presents itself as Blond.

Additional analysis conducted by listeners showed that a majority of the songs that appear on the album, such as “Nikes” and “Self Control,” are sung in a higher pitch, representing youthfulness and innocence. Furthermore, there are two versions of “Nikes:” the standard version and the physical version, which featured a third verse from Japanese rapper KOHH. The music video for “Nikes” also hints at the theme of duality, showcasing two versions of the McLaren F1 and its counterpart Longtail edition.

While many further theories explain the motif of duality and its correlation to Ocean, the beat switch is meant to encapsulate them all.

Throwing parties around England and mobbing freeways in four project M3s that I built with some friends.
